questions.question: How did the Brundtland Commission (1987) define sustainable development?
options: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
Maximising economic growth at any cost
Prioritising the present over the future
questions.explanation: The Brundtland Commission defined sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising future generations.

questions.question: What are the three pillars of sustainability?
questions.explanation: The three pillars of sustainability are environmental, economic and social sustainability.

questions.question: What is "greenwashing"?
options: Making misleading or false claims about environmental benefits
questions.explanation: Greenwashing is making misleading or false claims about the environmental benefits of a product, service or organisation.

questions.question: What does the "circular economy" aim to do?
options: Design out waste, keep materials in use and regenerate natural systems
questions.explanation: The circular economy offers an alternative to the linear "take-make-waste" model by designing out waste and keeping materials in use.

questions.question: Who chaired the Brundtland Commission?
options: Gro Harlem Brundtland, Norwegian Prime Minister
questions.explanation: The World Commission on Environment and Development was chaired by Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland.
